result.rationale: The diff shows post.rb's cook returning `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping Plugin::Filter and any sanitization. PollFeed feeds third-party RSS/Atom `i.content` into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This is a verifiable stored XSS path: unsanitized remote HTML is stored and rendered raw. The Readability tag whitelist in import_remote does not apply to the PollFeed path, and even whitelisted a/img with attributes is rendered raw.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and also skipping `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to third-party HTML (`contents` from RSS/Atom via `Jobs::PollFeed` using `i.content.scrub` and `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` using `Readability::Document#content`). None of these paths sanitize the HTML before storing it, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`; for `:raw_html`, `post.cooked == post.raw`. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff (arbitrary script/event-handler HTML from feeds/remote pages can be persisted and served to clients).
